topic: Why carbon forms a huge number of compounds
title: Why Carbon Forms Millions of Compounds
summary: Over 100 elements, yet most known compounds contain carbon. Four reasons, and why silicon can't do the same.

notes.title: 02 – Why Carbon Forms Millions of Compounds

keyPoints: **4 bonds:** one carbon atom can grow in 4 directions.
**Strong C–C bonds** (about 350 kJ/mol) make long chains stable; Si–Si bonds (about 225 kJ/mol) are weaker.
**Bond variety:** single, double and triple bonds, and easy bonds to O, N and halogens.
**Isomers:** C₄H₁₀ has 2, C₅H₁₂ has 3, C₁₀H₂₂ has 75, and C₂₀H₄₂ has 366,319.

quiz.q: Long silicon chains are less stable because:
options: Si–Si bonds are weaker than C–C bonds

quiz.q: How many isomers does C₅H₁₂ have?
Which is NOT a reason for the huge number of carbon compounds?

simulation.reason: Four facts about carbon: there is no variable to change here, and building isomers belongs to the isomerism topics that follow.
